ideas.title: The magnet stone that every nail feels
ideas.goal: In Jump in the player carries a magnet stone from the beach and sweeps it over the island: nails, the anchor chain and iron sand jump to it, hang from each other in chains, and fall off when the chain gets too heavy. Fun because every sweep finds something and the chains are never the same.
ideas.toward: Road step 1: one field for every iron thing, and soft iron that becomes a magnet itself when the stone is near (induced magnetisation, a volume solve), the base the coil and the motor need.
ideas.idea: physics/em.jl's mesh magnets plus soft iron: each iron body split into cells whose magnetisation solves M = chi H (demagnetising interactions included), forces and torques on every body from the same field, iron bodies as rigid bodies with contact. A nail tilts, slides and leaps to the stone; a second nail hangs from the first because the first is now a magnet.
ideas.form: A plugin: the magnet stone and iron things on the beach, picked up with a key in Jump in; a traced film of Lumi sweeping a nail trail out of the sand.

ideas.title: Paint with the field: iron filings on paper
ideas.goal: The player lays magnets under a sheet of paper, sprinkles iron filings on top and taps the paper: the filings stand up and chain along the field lines into patterns, and moving a magnet underneath redraws them. Fun as a toy to make pictures with that nobody has made before.
ideas.toward: Makes the invisible field the whole goal rests on visible, from the same solver, so every later machine can be checked by eye.
ideas.idea: Thousands of filings as tiny soft-iron needles on the GPU: each aligns with B, induces dipoles in its neighbours and chains; a tap shakes them loose (friction drops). Dark filings on white paper, path traced.
ideas.form: A table by the workshop; a traced top-down film of a pattern forming as the player slides a second magnet in.

ideas.title: Wind the coil yourself
ideas.goal: At the spindle the player cranks with the mouse and steers where the copper wire lands with the beak: neat turns side by side, or a sloppy heap. Then the coil goes on a cell and lifts as many nails as its real turns make field for. Fun to get good at: neat, many-turn coils lift the most, and the count shows how well you wound.
ideas.toward: Road step 5, and the critic's open point: what the player does minute to minute while the coil is wound.
ideas.idea: The wire is the wire.jl rod, laid onto the spindle where the beak guides it; the coil's field is Biot-Savart over the actual path it ended up in (em.jl force on a current path, reversed for the field), so overlaps and gaps change the pull.
ideas.form: A mini game at the workbench; a film of Lumi winding, then the nail stack test.

ideas.title: A cell from the sea: two metals in brine
ideas.goal: The player puts two different metals into a shell of seawater, joins them with a wire and feels what happens: a thin wire gets hot and glows, a thick one barely warms, a third shell in series makes more. Fun as the first time the player makes electricity out of things they found.
ideas.toward: Road step 4: a circuit that is found from what touches what, with voltage from the real metal pair and Joule heat from the real wire.
ideas.idea: Contacts between conductor bodies form a graph; a nodal solve gives each wire its current from the cell EMF (electrode potentials of the metals), internal resistance and the wire's own resistivity and cross-section; I^2 R heats each segment and its glow is emission by temperature.
ideas.form: A plugin by the tide pools; a traced night film of a thin copper wire glowing over three shells.

ideas.title: The wire you bent spins on the cell
ideas.goal: Any wire the player bends at the wire bench goes onto a cell standing on a magnet, and it spins, wobbles, stalls or flies off by its own shape. Fun because the player's own bends decide, and nobody has to type a shape in.
ideas.toward: Road step 6 in small: the human's complaint about the motor answered, a free 6-DOF wire pushed by the general field.
ideas.idea: The wire.jl rod as a free rigid body (6 DOF) on the cell's dimple and the magnet's rim with real contact; em.jl gives dF = I dl x B on every bit of it, current from the circuit solve; flying off happens when the contacts can no longer hold it, not at a speed limit.
ideas.form: On the wire bench in Jump in; a film of three wires the player bent, each doing something different.

ideas.title: Throw a nail with a coil: the timing game
ideas.goal: A coil on a tube pulls an iron nail in when the player closes the switch; let go at the right moment and the nail flies across the pond, too late and the coil sucks it back. Fun because it is a skill: the timing is everything, and the best shots land on the far bank.
ideas.toward: A first machine whose result depends on how the player works the field in time, the bridge to commutation in a motor.
ideas.idea: Field of the coil from em.jl, soft-iron nail magnetised by it, the switch as a circuit contact; the nail is a rigid body in the tube with friction; the shot length is what the field's work minus the suck-back gives.
ideas.form: A mini game at the pond; a slow-motion film of a perfect shot and a sucked-back one side by side.

ideas.title: A compass from a needle
ideas.goal: The player strokes a needle with the magnet stone, floats it on a leaf in a bowl of water, and it turns to the island's north. Then buried iron makes it swing, so the player finds hidden things with it. Fun as a tool the player made themselves and then uses to find something.
ideas.toward: Permanent magnetisation made by hand (hysteresis: stroking leaves remanence), and a weak island-wide field, both general parts of the solver.
ideas.idea: The needle's magnetisation grows with each stroke by a hysteresis model of steel; the island gets a uniform earth field; the leaf floats (hull.jl buoyancy) and turns by the torque m x B against water drag; buried iron adds its induced field.
ideas.form: A plugin with a bowl at the cottage; a film of the needle turning north, then swinging over a buried anchor.

ideas.title: The slow magnet: drop it down a copper pipe
ideas.goal: The player drops a magnet down three pipes they made, wood, iron and copper: through wood it falls, iron grabs it, and in copper it sinks slowly as if in honey. Fun because it looks impossible and the player can try any pipe they make.
ideas.toward: Induction from the same fields (road step 7 needs it): currents the moving field makes in a conductor, and their push back.
ideas.idea: Eddy currents in the pipe wall from the changing flux (the wall as rings of conductor, each with its own EMF -d(phi)/dt and resistance), their field acting back on the magnet; the fall speed comes out of the copper's resistivity and the wall's thickness.
ideas.form: A pipe stand at the workshop; a traced film of three magnets dropped at once.

ideas.title: Copper from green rock
ideas.goal: The player breaks green rock from the cliff, roasts it in the kiln with charcoal, and pours the copper that melts out into a stone mould, then pulls the bar through a die into wire of the thickness they choose. Fun because the wire the player winds later is wire they made from a stone.
ideas.toward: Road step 3: materials that come from the island, with their real melting point and the wire's real thickness carried into the circuit.
ideas.idea: Heat in the kiln as a lumped thermal model per piece, malachite reduced above its temperature with charcoal; molten copper flows into the mould (a small Maelstrom pour or a height field); drawing through the die is wire.jl's plasticity with work hardening.
ideas.form: A plugin at the kiln and the cliff; a film from rock to glowing pour to a coil of wire.

ideas.title: Crank the dynamo and feel the lamp
ideas.goal: The player turns a crank with the mouse to light a lamp: with the lamp off the crank spins easily, switch it on and it gets hard to turn, and a brighter lamp is harder still. Fun because the player feels electricity as weight in their hand.
ideas.toward: Road step 7: a motor turned backwards makes current, from the same fields and circuit, and the load pushes back on the hand.
ideas.idea: A coil turning in the magnet's field: EMF from the changing flux through its real turns, current from the circuit with the lamp's resistance, the torque back on the crank from I dl x B; the lamp's glow from its filament's Joule heat.
ideas.form: A crank at the cottage door; a night film of Lumi cranking and the lamp brightening as it strains.
